title: Metaphase preparation from murine bone marrow
protocol: Warm 0.06M potassium chloride in a 37°C water bath.
Inject 250 μL of 200 μg/mL colcemid into the peritoneum of mice and arrest cell cycle for 30 minutes.
Flush bone marrow cells with 30 mL pre-warmed 0.06M potassium chloride into a 50 mL tube through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Rock sample tubes gently in a 37°C incubator for 20 min.
Make fixative solution (methanol : glacial acetic acid = 3:1) during hypotonic incubation.
Add 2 mL Fixative into samples and mix gently.
Centrifuge at 1500 rpm for 7 min and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells thoroughly with 0.5 mL 0.06M potassium chloride.
Add few drops of fixative to cells and mix well.
Keep adding and mixing fixative drops into cells until reaching 3 mL.
Add fixative up to 20 mL in total, mix by inversion, and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Run the sample mixture through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge at 1500 rpm for 7 min and discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellets in 20 mL fixative and incubate at room temperature for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 1500 rpm for 7 min and discard supernatant.
Repeat step of resuspending pellets in 20 mL fixative, incubating for 10 min, and centrifuging for 7 min.
Resuspend cell pellets in 2 mL fixative and store at -20°C for long-term storage.
Use the flame method or other methods to spread and stain chromosomes on slides.
Drop 30 μL of fixed cells onto pre-cleaned and wet slides tilted at a 45-degree angle.
Put slides in burner flame for 2 seconds to allow chromosomes to spread out.
Let slides dry completely.
Dilute 20x Giemsa stain with water to prepare a 1x Giemsa solution.
Stain chromosome-spread slides with 1x Giemsa solution for 5 minutes.
Wash off the Giemsa solution and let slides dry.
Check chromosome quality under a microscope.
